name: window.state
description: Report whether the window is minimised, maximised, normal, or hidden. Read-only; for state changes use window.move (size) or future window.minimise / window.maximise verbs.

state.description: Current window state. `hidden` means the window has WS_VISIBLE clear (not just minimised).

x-implementations.name: get_window_placement
x-implementations.description: Win32 `IsWindowVisible` (test for `hidden`) + `GetWindowPlacement` (`SW_SHOWMINIMIZED`/`SW_SHOWMAXIMIZED`/`SW_SHOWNORMAL`). Maps the Win32 showCmd values to the spec's four states.

windows-modern.description: IsWindowVisible + GetWindowPlacement. The `hidden` state is reported even for windows that ARE actually minimised but lack WS_VISIBLE — visibility takes precedence over placement.

windows-classic.description: Same Win32 APIs (available NT 3.1+). Identical state-mapping behaviour as windows-modern.
